To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
it is possible to provide service differentiation in IEEE 802,11e EDCA by tuning only one parameter, the contention window size, while keeping the AIFS values fixed for all traffic classes.

by assigning appropriate values to the contention window sizes, the AIFS values, and/or the TXOP values for different traffic classes, it is possible to achieve (proportional or absolute) service differentiation and maximize the total system capacity, and the design dimension should not be kept large by turning multiple sets of parameters.

(i) the contention window sizes of different classes should be set to different values to provide service differentiation and (ii) it is desirable to keep the number of parameters that can be tuned to a minimum (i.e., to tune only the contention window sizes) in order to achieve high channel utilization and QoS guarantees.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a practical and effective mechanism that can be used by the EDCA to support differentiated services and maximize system utilization.

the following issues in IEEE 80211e: (1) how to tune the parameters of IEEE 80211E EDCA in order to achieve service differentiation and maximize the channel utilization, (2) how to incorporate the theoretical results into IEEE802.11e, and (3) how to practically implement the proposed approach on real wireless devices.
the design and implementation of adaptive and differentiated QoS in WLANs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach can achieve the targeted throughput ratios among the different traffic classes, and at the same time maximize the system capacity.
, in order to achieve QoS differentiation among multiple traffic classes, it is not necessary to tune all the parameters in EDCA.
our study has demonstrated that, by tuning parameters in IEEE 11e EDCA, it is indeed possible to provide service differentiation and achieve the targeted throughput ratios among classes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the analytical models developed for IEEE 802.1l EDCA can serve as a useful tool to guide practical design and configuration of EDCA parameters.
the proposed model can be used as an effective analytical tool to guide the tuning of EDCA parameters in a WLAN to achieve the desired service differentiation and high throughput.

the analytical model and the proposed approaches can be used as a tool for designing, analyzing, and tuning the IEEE 802. 11e EDCA protocol, and thus, can be used to guide the design and development of future WLANs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by tuning only the contention window size of each traffic class, it is feasible, through the derived theoretical model, to provide service differentiation and at the same time maximize the system throughput.
the analytical model can be used as an important tool to study the performance of the enhanced distributed channel access mechanism and to provide guidance for the design of practical WLAN systems.
, by carefully tuning the contention window size, it is possible to provide service differentiation among different traffic classes and achieve high channel utilization in WLANs.
